mismatches.detail: RULINGS.md states it 'buckets every screen' and totals 91 across its 4 buckets, but at least 4 live, routed screens have zero mention anywhere in the document: kyc/kyc_checklist_screen.dart (/kyc/checklist -- the KYC flow's own 'spine' screen, s11), onboarding/whats_next_screen.dart (/onboarding/next-steps, s07), onboarding/legal_preview_screen.dart's LegalBundlePreviewScreen (/legal-preview, a second class in an already-ruled file), and markets/price_alerts_screen.dart's SetPriceAlertScreen (/asset/:ticker/alert, s49, a second class in an already-ruled file). All 4 have canvas artboard ids cited directly in routes.dart comments that DO exist in the verified 135-artboard set, so this isn't a case of genuinely-undesigned surfaces -- the ruling sheet simply never evaluated them.
mismatches.hides: The two file-sharing cases (bundle preview, set-price-alert) mean file-level granularity in RULINGS.md silently swallows a whole second route -- so '91 ruled screens' overstates coverage even before counting the KYC-spine and onboarding-completion gaps, which are outright absent. A reviewer who treats RULINGS.md as the authoritative screen census (as this audit's own brief initially assumed by using it as the backbone for source 3) undercounts the true screen surface and has no ruling on record for two of the app's most heavily-trafficked screens -- every single onboarding investor passes through both kyc_checklist and whats_next.

mismatches.detail: kyc/next_of_kin.dart (route /kyc/next-of-kin, step 8 of 8 -- the LAST KYC collection step; its own 'Submit for verification' button calls finalizeDraft() directly, ending onboarding) has zero screenshots in build/shots/, in either theme. The step immediately before it (kyc_declarations) and immediately after it (kyc_submitted) both have full light+dark captures -- the harness walks past this exact step without capturing it.
mismatches.hides: Nobody has visually verified the screen every investor must complete to submit their KYC application at all. A reviewer scanning the shot set by KYC step number would see an unbroken sequence and wrongly conclude the whole 8-step flow was checked.

mismatches.detail: wallet/wallet_flows.dart's normal-hours Withdraw sheet (_WithdrawSheet, UNROUTED via showWithdrawFlow(), artboards s37/s30 per RULINGS.md redesign-to-artboard) has no capture. Its rarer sibling -- the outside-hours/queued variant (_OutsideHoursWithdrawSheet) -- IS captured twice (withdraw_outside_hours_pin, withdraw_outside_hours_s37variant), and withdraw_mandate (an unrelated DCS-mandate screen) is captured too.
mismatches.hides: The withdraw path used on every weekday between roughly 09:00 and 21:00 -- i.e. most of the time money actually leaves the app -- has never been visually checked, while the edge-case path that only fires outside those hours has. A reviewer searching shots for 'withdraw' finds two hits and reasonably assumes withdraw is covered.

mismatches.detail: 22 of the 39 rows RULINGS.md buckets as 'needs-ruling' (i.e. 'no artboard covers these') carry evidence text in that same row citing a specific matching artboard id -- e.g. onboarding/create_passcode_screen.dart's own evidence says s05 '...matches the app screen', welcome_slider_screen.dart cites s02, wallet_screens.dart#transaction_detail cites s38 ('found in s38...matching the app's own Reference row'). The bucket assignment does not reliably track the evidence column within the same document.
mismatches.hides: The document's own headline split (39 needs-ruling / 28 redesign-to-artboard) overstates how much of the product is actually undesigned. A reader trusting only the bucket counts, not the evidence prose, would misjudge design coverage in both directions -- underestimating how many screens have a real artboard, and not noticing which specific rows to double check.

mismatches.detail: Artboard s38 is independently claimed as the covering artboard for TWO structurally different screens: account/contract_note_screen.dart (bucketed redesign-to-artboard, confidence 'likely', 'closest new-canvas expression of a post-trade receipt') and wallet/wallet_screens.dart#transaction_detail (bucketed needs-ruling, evidence: 'Reference'/'Fees, all in' rows found in s38). One is marked resolved, the other is not, off the same artboard evidence.
mismatches.hides: Whether s38 was actually designed as a wallet-transaction receipt, a per-order contract note, or was never meant to serve both -- the two screens have different data (a wallet Txn vs an executed order) and the ruling sheet does not record which one the artboard is really for.

mismatches.detail: Routes.acctComplaintTracked (/account/help/complaint/tracked, ComplaintTrackedScreen) is a fully registered GoRoute -- app_router.dart's own comment says 'no live entry point yet -- submitting a complaint has no real backend to return one from ... registered so the built screen is reachable once that exists.' It appears in the shot set (63_complaint_tracked) only because the capture harness can drive a route directly, bypassing the missing in-app trigger.
mismatches.hides: Counting this as 'routed' (source 1) or 'captured' makes it look reachable through the real app when it is not -- the inverse of the UNROUTED-but-reachable-by-sheet problem this audit was asked to watch for. A route in app_router.dart does not by itself prove a real user can ever land on the screen.

mismatches.detail: RULINGS.md's no-action bucket (dated 2026-08-26) describes account/tax_documents_screen.dart as 'currently unreachable from any live UI in the app itself (hidden by dir[ect instruction])'. account_screen.dart's own code comment says the menu row was 'Restored 2026-08-27' -- one day later -- because the backend gained the tax statement kinds it needed; it is now a live, wired, real-backend-calling route (/account/tax) with a permanent Account-menu entry.

It is in fact a live, reachable, real-data screen with zero artboard anywhere in the canvas -- it should be in restyle-only, not no-action, and nobody has ruled on its design treatment.

mismatches.detail: RULINGS.md's own header states 'Nothing in the build queue starts until the needs-ruling section is empty,' and its needs-ruling table has an empty 'your ruling' column for all 39 rows. DECISIONS.md, dated the same day (2026-08-26) through 2026-08-27, contains explicit product-owner rulings (R-1, R-1a, R-6, R-8, R-8a, R-9, R-10, R-11, R-12, R-14, R-15/R-32, R-16 through R-25, R-33) that resolve essentially every one of the 39 rows -- and the build has visibly proceeded past that gate (76 routes exist, 236 screenshots captured, commit history shows 'Wave 6' etc.).
mismatches.hides: Someone reading only RULINGS.md, exactly as the task brief warns against ('sources that do not read each other'), would conclude the project is still blocked on 39 open product decisions. The actual resolutions live in a second document and were never written back into RULINGS.md's own ruling column, so the two documents tell contradictory stories about whether the build gate is open.

mismatches.detail: routes.dart and app_router.dart comments cite 'Screen 65' (acctWithdrawMandate), 'Screen 66' (contractNote), 'screens 76-97', 'screens 81-84', 'screen 85' (acctTax), 'screen 86' (priceAlerts), 'screens 87-88' (complaint), 'screens 89, 90, 92', 'screen 91', and 'screens 94-97' -- all from a 97-light-screen OLD canvas that DECISIONS.md itself records was replaced by the current 56-artboard canvas (verified: the current canvas's highest sNN id is s58, with only 56 base-numbered screens, gaps at 28 and 32). mismatches.hides: Nothing new is hidden -- R-5 already flags this -- but the stale numbers are still live in the source as of this audit (confirmed by my own grep), so any future agent or engineer who reads a route comment without first reading R-5 will misidentify which artboard, if any, actually covers that screen.

mismatches.detail: docs/redesign/canvas-inventory.json's total of 135 is correct against my own regex parse of the 6 numbered .dc.html files (56 base screens x light/dark + variant states = 135, verified independently). But two more .dc.html files sit in the same docs/design/redesign-2026-08/ folder -- 'Home Variants.dc.html' (ids '3e', 'l1': alternate home-screen treatments, e.g. 'Dark - approved') and 'Landing Video Concept.dc.html' (ids 'v1'/'v2'/'v3'/'kd-landing-still': marketing video-concept frames, one of which -- V3 -- is the actual ruling for the Welcome screen per DECISIONS.md R-14). Neither file's ids match the sNN pattern the inventory script looks for, so both are invisible to it.
mismatches.hides: R-14 (Welcome screen) rules in favor of an artboard that the pre-parsed inventory doesn't know exists at all. Anyone using canvas-inventory.json as the complete artboard index would never find the artboard the product owner actually chose for Welcome.
